• Core fact: Rajaraja I (r. 985–1014 CE) invaded Ceylon (Sri Lanka) around 993 CE, defeated King Mahinda V, destroyed the capital Anuradhapura, and annexed its northern half as a Chola province named Mummudi Chola Mandalam.
• Option A is incorrect: Aditya I (r. 871–907 CE) expanded the Chola kingdom by defeating the Pallava ruler Aparajita and the Western Gangas, but did not mount a naval campaign against Ceylon.
• Option C is incorrect: Rajendra I (r. 1014–1044 CE) completed the conquest of the entirety of Ceylon in 1017 CE, capturing the Sinhala king Mahinda V along with the royal jewels, rather than initiating the first conquest.
• Option D is incorrect: Vijayalaya (r. c. 850–871 CE) re-established the imperial Chola dynasty by capturing Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars; his realm was confined to the Kaveri delta.
• Often confused with: Rajendra I vs. Rajaraja I — Rajaraja I conquered northern Ceylon (setting up Polonnaruwa as the administrative seat), whereas his son Rajendra I extended Chola control to the whole island.
issues_found: Ambiguity in historical phrasing: Rajaraja I conquered northern Ceylon (c. 993 CE), while Rajendra I conquered the entire island (1017 CE), leading to frequent confusion between Options B and C.
